title: The people answer
summary: King Benjamin sends among the people to learn whether they believe his words. The people answer together, describing their changed hearts, knowledge, joy, and willingness to covenant with God.

explicit_facts.text: King Benjamin sent among the people to learn whether they believed his words.
The people answered with one voice that they believed his words and attributed their changed hearts to the Spirit of the Lord Omnipotent.
The people said they had great views of what was to come and rejoiced because of their faith in the king's words.
The people expressed willingness to covenant with God and obey his commandments throughout their lives.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people speak together in response to King Benjamin.
unspecified_visual_details: The physical setting, architecture, clothing, crowd arrangement, and individual appearance are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Yea, we believe all the words which thou hast spoken unto us;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the people

spoken_dialogue.text: we have no more disposition to do evil, but to do good continually.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the people

spoken_dialogue.text: And we are willing to enter into a covenant with our God to do his will,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The people's changed hearts and covenant are reported in their speech; do not depict them as visible supernatural effects.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the Spirit as a visible figure or force.
Do not invent a ceremony or physical covenant act.

title: Benjamin affirms the covenant
summary: King Benjamin tells the people that they have spoken the words he desired and that their covenant is righteous. He teaches that through the covenant they are called the children of Christ.

explicit_facts.text: King Benjamin tells the people that they have spoken the words he desired and made a righteous covenant.
King Benjamin teaches that the people who made the covenant are called the children of Christ and that their hearts are changed through faith in Christ's name.

reasonable_visual_inferences: King Benjamin addresses the assembled people.
unspecified_visual_details: The physical setting, gestures, clothing, and arrangement of the people are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: and the covenant which ye have made is a righteous covenant.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

spoken_dialogue.text: ye shall be called the children of Christ, his sons, and his daughters;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Children of Christ” and spiritual begetting are teachings, not literal visible transformations.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ as physically present; his appearance is not narrated here.

title: Take upon you the name of Christ
summary: King Benjamin teaches that the people should take upon them the name of Christ and contrasts being called by Christ's name with being called by another name.

explicit_facts.text: King Benjamin teaches that the people who covenant should take upon them the name of Christ and remain obedient.
He says that those who take upon them Christ's name will be found at God's right hand and those who do not will be at God's left hand.

reasonable_visual_inferences: King Benjamin continues speaking to the people.
unspecified_visual_details: No actual judgment scene, divine figure, or right-and-left placement is described as occurring in the present.

title: Retain the name in your hearts
summary: King Benjamin urges the people to remember and retain Christ's name in their hearts, warning against transgression and teaching that a person cannot know a master whom they have not served.

explicit_facts.text: King Benjamin says the name he gave the people should not be blotted out except through transgression and urges them not to transgress.
He urges them to retain the name in their hearts and teaches that one cannot know a master whom one has not served.

reasonable_visual_inferences: King Benjamin continues his address to the people.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, visual representation of a name in the heart, and any master figure are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: For how knoweth a man the master whom he has not served,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The name written in hearts is figurative teaching, not a visible inscription.

title: The neighbor's ass
summary: King Benjamin asks whether a man would take and keep his neighbor's ass, then uses the example to teach what happens when people do not know the name by which they are called.

explicit_facts.text: King Benjamin asks whether a man would keep his neighbor's ass and says the man would not even allow it to feed among his flocks, but would drive it away.
King Benjamin applies the example to those who do not know the name by which they are called.

reasonable_visual_inferences: King Benjamin gives the example while addressing the people.
unspecified_visual_details: The ass, neighbor, flocks, and any action involving them are presented as a rhetorical example, not a narrated event; their appearance and setting are unspecified.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The ass-and-flock comparison is a rhetorical teaching; do not stage it as a separate event.

title: Steadfast in good works
summary: King Benjamin exhorts the people to be steadfast and abound in good works, teaching that Christ may seal them his and bring them to everlasting salvation and eternal life. He concludes, “Amen.”

explicit_facts.text: King Benjamin urges the people to be steadfast, immovable, and always abound in good works.
He teaches that Christ may seal them his and that they may receive everlasting salvation and eternal life.

reasonable_visual_inferences: King Benjamin delivers the concluding exhortation to the people.
unspecified_visual_details: No visible sealing, ascent to heaven, or depiction of Christ is described.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The promised sealing and salvation are teachings, not visible events in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a supernatural sealing, ascent, or Christ appearing.
